subject: Reasoning
description: Identify correct overlap pattern for given category triples

questions.stem: Which Venn relationship best describes the categories DOCTORS, ENGINEERS, MEN?

options.option_text: All three are mutually exclusive (no overlap)
Doctors and Engineers don't overlap with each other; both partially overlap with Men (some doctors are men; some engineers are men)

questions.explanation: A doctor cannot also be an engineer in the same instant of practice — these are different professions. So no overlap between Doctors and Engineers. But both groups have men → both intersect with the 'Men' set. Standard Venn — Two non-overlapping circles (Doctors, Engineers), each partially inside a larger 'Men' circle. Symbolically — D ∩ E = ∅, D ∩ M ≠ ∅, E ∩ M ≠ ∅.

questions.stem: Which is the best Venn relation for: ANIMALS, DOGS, CATS?

options.option_text: All three concentric (one inside the other)
Dogs and Cats are non-overlapping subsets of Animals

questions.explanation: Dogs ⊂ Animals; Cats ⊂ Animals; Dogs ∩ Cats = ∅ (a single creature can't be both). So two smaller circles (Dogs, Cats) sit inside a larger circle (Animals), with no overlap between Dogs and Cats. Pattern called 'two non-overlapping subsets of a common superset'. Compare 'Mango, Banana, Fruit' (same pattern); 'Doctor, Engineer, Person' (same pattern).

questions.stem: Pick the correct Venn relation for: STUDENTS, CRICKETERS, BOOKS:

options.option_text: Students and Cricketers overlap (some students play cricket); Books has no overlap with either (Books are inanimate objects)

questions.explanation: Students ∩ Cricketers ≠ ∅ (some students are cricketers; some cricketers are students). Books ∩ Students = ∅ (a person and an object cannot share identity). Books ∩ Cricketers = ∅. So two partly-overlapping circles (Students, Cricketers) with a separate disjoint circle for Books. Common in 'mixed-category' Venn questions — the inanimate-vs-animate test is a quick check for disjoint relations.

questions.stem: Best Venn relation for: WHEAT, BARLEY, GRAIN?

options.option_text: Wheat and Barley are non-overlapping subsets of Grain
All three overlap with same area

questions.explanation: Wheat ⊂ Grain; Barley ⊂ Grain; Wheat ∩ Barley = ∅. Two smaller non-overlapping circles inside a larger 'Grain' circle. Same pattern as 'Cars, Trucks, Vehicles', 'Lions, Tigers, Felines'.

questions.stem: Best Venn relation for: TEACHERS, SCIENTISTS, INDIANS?

options.option_text: All three overlap pairwise — some Teachers are Scientists; some Indians are Teachers; some Indians are Scientists

questions.explanation: All three pairs have non-empty intersections. Some Teachers ARE Scientists (e.g., a professor researching). Some Indians are Teachers. Some Indians are Scientists. Some Indians are both Teachers AND Scientists (the central triple-intersection). So the standard 3-way overlapping Venn (the 7-region diagram) applies. Set theory — union of 3 sets has up to 2³ − 1 = 7 disjoint regions.

questions.stem: What is the best Venn relation for: TABLE, CHAIR, FURNITURE?

options.option_text: All three concentric (one inside another inside another)
Table and Chair are non-overlapping subsets of Furniture (a piece of furniture is either a table or a chair, not both)

questions.explanation: Table ⊂ Furniture; Chair ⊂ Furniture; Table ∩ Chair = ∅. Two non-overlapping subsets of a larger superset. Identical pattern to 'Wheat, Barley, Grain' or 'Dogs, Cats, Animals'. Quick spot — the umbrella term is one element + the other two are types of it that don't blend.

questions.stem: If 60 students play cricket, 40 play football and 20 play both, how many play AT LEAST ONE?
questions.explanation: Inclusion-Exclusion: |A ∪ B| = |A| + |B| − |A ∩ B| = 60 + 40 − 20 = 80. 80 students play at least one. Of these — 60 play cricket (40 only-cricket + 20 both); 40 play football (20 only-football + 20 both); 20 play both. The trap option 100 fails to subtract the double-counted overlap.
